newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB warns against excessive expectations.
newsitem.headline: ABB warns against excessive expectations.

text.p: ABB AG, the Swiss company that owns half of electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, on Thursday warned against overly optimistic profit expectations and said the recent drop in its share price was hard to comprehend.

Bernd Mueller-Berghoff, vice-president of ABB AG, said he was concerned that many people no longer understood the enormous efforts required of ABB to achieve its 1996 results in extremely competitive surroundings.
ABB, and other publicly quoted companies, had recorded a very good performance over the last few years, but it is becoming increasingly tough to live up to high expectations.
"It is becoming increasingly difficult to fulfil such expectations," Mueller-Berghoff said, referring to analysts' optimistic forecast for ABB's profits in 1996.

Mueller-Berghoff told the annual shareholders' meeting of Swiss ABB AG that the recent fall in its share price was difficult to comprehend in light of the 16 percent rise in 1996 profits and a 27 percent hike in the dividend.
"Following the ABB news conference and the publication of our results there were setbacks because the statements were partly seen as disappointing," Mueller-Berghoff said.
Earlier this year ABB reported a 6.2 percent fall in its group net profit to $1.233 billion. However, on a comparable basis profit actually rose 15.8 percent.
The 1995 result was inflated by a one-off payment of $250 million and ABB had always said the extraordinary gain should be disregarded.
However, many analysts immediately cut their forecasts and downgraded ABB's shares because the 1996 result was below their expectations and ABB's forecast for 1997 was less than rosy.
Since the publication of its results at the end of February, the shares of ABB's Swiss quoted parent company have lost 7.9 percent and closed 14 francs lower on Thursday.
Analysts have openly admitted they had been overly optimistic about ABB's prospects and turned a deaf ear to the company's repeated warnings about 1996.
ABB's forecast for 1997, which was repeated at today's annual meeting of ABB AG in Switzerland, calls for net profit for 1997 to at least reach the 1996 level.
